author: Smoebo
subjectBasis: The young, adult and ancient dragons of the ten SRD 5.1 colours, as original designs per docs/art/creature-art-guidance.md. The SRD gives each dragon numbers and a breath weapon and no description of its looks, so the head shapes are invented and no published illustration was named or supplied.
why: The plates these replace (docs/art/core-monster-plates-2026-11-18.json) did not tell the ages apart: an ancient was often the dimmest of its three. Each age is now painted to a rule that survives at token size. Young: lean, in profile, short horns, about 65 percent of the frame on a bright backdrop, a wisp of breath. Adult: heavy-jawed, a full crown of horns, about 85 percent of the frame, its breath pouring out. Ancient: seen from the front and from below, a scarred head lowered toward the viewer with shoulders and wings behind it, on a dark backdrop. A colour keeps its hue at every age; age shows as wear at the edges, so a copper dragon is still read as copper at 40px.
review: Each plate was viewed as a full square and as a round crop at 96px and 40px on dark and light. The ancients were painted four times: the first ran their horns into the corners the round crop cuts, the second came back on a painted disc, three of the third sat on a backdrop of their own colour, and all of the third were heads with no body, which Albert caught. The young red and blue were painted twice for a neck that ended in mid-air, and the ancient blue once more for a body that faded out at the bottom edge. The wyrmlings are unchanged.
